topic: Belgium's Vennbahn and 6 more strange borders
hook: Your cycle path is Belgian land, but German villages sit on both sides of it.
title: A Belgian Path Cuts Through Germany: 7 Odd Borders
description:
A Belgian cycle path runs through Germany, and that is only border number seven. Count down seven real borders that make no sense, from a German village surrounded by Switzerland to a lake with no agreed border, ending on a strange enclave right here in India. Every place is real and you can check it on a map.

#borders #geography #facts

scenes.narration: Your cycle path is Belgian land, but German villages sit on both sides of it.
scenes.headline: Belgium Inside Germany

scenes.narration: That is real, and it is only border number seven. Today we count down seven borders that make no sense.
scenes.headline: 7 Borders

scenes.narration: Each one is stranger than the last, and the number one border is right here in India.
scenes.headline: Number One Is Indian

scenes.narration: By the end, you will see a piece of land inside a piece of land, inside another piece of land.
scenes.headline: Land Inside Land

scenes.narration: On the way, you will meet a village with two currencies and a town trapped inside France.
scenes.headline: Two Currencies

scenes.narration: You will also see a lake that three countries have never agreed how to divide.
scenes.headline: A Lake, Three Countries

scenes.narration: Stay till the end, because the last border was only fixed in 2015, after a deal between India and Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Fixed in 2015

scenes.narration: Number seven. The Vennbahn, a railway built more than a hundred years ago, when this whole area belonged to Germany.
scenes.headline: The Vennbahn

scenes.narration: It carried coal and steel between German cities and Luxembourg, running through quiet green hills near the Belgian border.
scenes.headline: A Coal Railway

scenes.narration: Then Germany lost the First World War, and the peace treaty of 1919 handed that railway line to Belgium.
scenes.headline: Handed To Belgium

scenes.narration: Belgium got the track, but not the land around it. So a thin Belgian strip now runs through German ground.
scenes.headline: A Thin Belgian Strip

scenes.narration: Today the trains are gone. The old line is a famous cycle path, about 125 kilometres long.
scenes.headline: A Cycle Path Now

scenes.narration: The route also reaches Luxembourg, so one old railway line links three countries today.
scenes.headline: Three Countries

scenes.narration: You ride on Belgian land, while German villages like Mützenich sit beside you, on both sides of the path.
scenes.headline: German Villages Both Sides

scenes.narration: Think about it. You stay on a path owned by one country, while the villages next to you belong to another.
scenes.headline: One Path, Two Owners

scenes.narration: There is no wall and no passport check, because both countries are in Europe's open-border zone.
scenes.headline: No Border Check

scenes.narration: So the map changed after a war, and a railway stayed behind as a Belgian strip in Germany.
scenes.headline: A War Redrew It

scenes.narration: Strange? Yes. But number six is stranger, because it is a whole village that is surrounded by another country.
scenes.headline: Next: A Whole Village

scenes.narration: Number six. Büsingen, a German village completely surrounded by Switzerland.
scenes.headline: Büsingen

scenes.narration: Look at the map, and you see a small German pocket, with Swiss land on every side.
scenes.headline: A German Pocket

scenes.narration: It sits on the Rhine river, near the Swiss city of Schaffhausen, so Switzerland really is all around it.
scenes.headline: Swiss On Every Side

scenes.narration: The people there are German citizens, so they follow German law and vote in German elections.
scenes.headline: German Citizens

scenes.narration: But the village sits inside the Swiss customs area, and both euros and Swiss francs are used there.
scenes.headline: Euros And Francs

scenes.narration: Two countries' money, in one small village. That is rare for any place on Earth.
scenes.headline: Two Currencies

scenes.narration: To reach the rest of Germany by road, you have to cross Swiss land first.
scenes.headline: Road Through Switzerland

scenes.narration: Imagine a village in one Indian state, where every road out passes through a different country. That is daily life here.
scenes.headline: Imagine It In India

scenes.narration: Small, quiet, and perfectly normal for the people who live there, yet it looks like a mistake on the map.
scenes.headline: Looks Like A Mistake

scenes.narration: But a piece of America is stuck on the wrong side of a border too.
scenes.headline: Next: America's Pocket

scenes.narration: And that one begins with a map that was simply wrong.
scenes.headline: A Map That Was Wrong

scenes.narration: Number five. The Northwest Angle, a small piece of Minnesota that sits north of the rest of the United States.
scenes.headline: Northwest Angle

scenes.narration: On a map it looks like a mistake, a little box of America stuck on top of Canada.
scenes.headline: A Box On Top

scenes.narration: To drive there from the rest of Minnesota, you must go through Canada, because no road connects it by land.
scenes.headline: Drive Through Canada

scenes.narration: So an American has to enter Canada, and then come back into the United States on the same trip.
scenes.headline: Leave And Re-enter

scenes.narration: Why? In 1783, the treaty makers used a map that was wrong about the lakes and rivers.
scenes.headline: A Wrong Map, 1783

scenes.narration: They believed the Mississippi river began farther north than it really does, and they drew the line using that idea.
scenes.headline: Wrong About The River

scenes.narration: The mistake was never undone, so this corner of America ended up cut off from the rest by land.
scenes.headline: Cut Off By Land

scenes.narration: Much of it is lake and forest, so the real way in is often by boat or plane.
scenes.headline: Boat Or Plane

scenes.narration: One wrong map, and a whole corner of a country was cut off. Next, a whole town goes the same way.
scenes.headline: Next: A Trapped Town

scenes.narration: Number four. Llívia, a Spanish town that sits inside France.
scenes.headline: Llívia

scenes.narration: Spain is only a few kilometres away, but between the town and Spain lies French land.
scenes.headline: French Land Between

scenes.narration: This goes back to 1659, when Spain gave several villages to France in the Treaty of the Pyrenees.
scenes.headline: Treaty Of The Pyrenees

scenes.narration: But Llívia counted as a town, not a village, so it stayed Spanish. One word on paper decided the border.
scenes.headline: One Word Decided It

scenes.narration: Today a road called the neutral road connects Llívia to Spain. The land is French, but a Spanish road runs across it.
scenes.headline: The Neutral Road

scenes.narration: If you like strange places like these, this is a good moment to subscribe, because there are more to come.
scenes.headline: Subscribe For More

scenes.narration: So a Spanish town lives inside France, with its own fields, its own streets and a Spanish name on the map.
scenes.headline: A Spanish Island

scenes.narration: Now imagine that, but with an entire region, big enough to be a small country.
scenes.headline: Now A Whole Region

scenes.narration: Number three is not a town at all, and it belongs to one of the biggest countries on Earth.
scenes.headline: A Giant's Odd Piece

scenes.narration: Number three. Kaliningrad, a part of Russia that is not connected to the rest of Russia.
scenes.headline: Kaliningrad

scenes.narration: It sits on the Baltic coast, with Poland on one side and Lithuania on the other.
scenes.headline: Between Poland And Lithuania

scenes.narration: Poland and Lithuania are both in the European Union, so this is a Russian region surrounded by EU land and sea.
scenes.headline: Surrounded By The EU

scenes.narration: This land used to be a German city called Königsberg, until the Soviet Union took it after the Second World War.
scenes.headline: Once Königsberg

scenes.narration: Today, travel by road or train from there to the rest of Russia means passing through other countries.
scenes.headline: Pass Through Others

scenes.narration: Imagine if Goa belonged to India, but every road to the rest of India passed through another country.
scenes.headline: Imagine Goa Cut Off

scenes.narration: That is what Russia lives with in Kaliningrad, a piece of the country that cannot be reached by land alone.
scenes.headline: Not Reachable By Land

scenes.narration: A piece of land cut off from its country. Now, what about a border that is missing from the map?
scenes.headline: Next: A Missing Border

scenes.narration: Number two does not even have a line on the map in the middle of the water.
scenes.headline: No Line On Water

scenes.narration: Number two. Lake Constance, where three countries share one lake, and nobody has agreed where the borders lie.
scenes.headline: Lake Constance

scenes.narration: Germany, Switzerland and Austria all touch its shores. It sits near the Alps and is hugely popular with tourists.
scenes.headline: Germany, Swiss, Austria

scenes.narration: On land, the borders are clear. On the water, there is no officially agreed line.
scenes.headline: No Line On The Water

scenes.narration: The three countries hold different views on how the lake should be divided, and that question is still open.
scenes.headline: Still Not Agreed

scenes.narration: Boats, fishing and rescue are handled by practical agreements, so everyday life carries on without trouble.
scenes.headline: Life Carries On

scenes.narration: So you can sail across it, and never know which country's water you are floating on.
scenes.headline: Whose Water?

scenes.narration: A border that is clear on land, and simply fades away at the water's edge.
scenes.headline: A Fading Border

scenes.narration: Now for the one I promised, because it is the strangest border on this list, and it is in India.
scenes.headline: Now, India

scenes.narration: Number one. Cooch Behar in West Bengal, near the Bangladesh border.
scenes.headline: Cooch Behar

scenes.narration: Until 2015, this area was full of tiny islands of land, each belonging to the other country.
scenes.headline: Islands Of Land

scenes.narration: There were 111 Indian enclaves inside Bangladesh, and 51 Bangladeshi enclaves inside India.
scenes.headline: 111 And 51

scenes.narration: Some were just a few fields big. People lived there as citizens of a country they could not easily reach.
scenes.headline: A Few Fields Big

scenes.narration: Many struggled to get schools, hospitals or electricity, because the country around them was not their own.
scenes.headline: No Easy Access

scenes.narration: Think of the people. For decades, they lived on land that the official maps called foreign.
scenes.headline: Foreign On The Map

scenes.narration: And the strangest of them all was called Dahala Khagrabari.
scenes.headline: Dahala Khagrabari

scenes.narration: It was an Indian plot, inside a Bangladeshi plot, inside an Indian plot, inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Land In Land In Land

scenes.narration: Experts called it the world's only third-order enclave. Standing there, you were in India, inside Bangladesh, inside India, inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: A World Record

scenes.narration: On the night of 31 July 2015, India and Bangladesh finally swapped the enclaves, and people could choose their country.
scenes.headline: The Midnight Swap

scenes.narration: After nearly seventy years, the maps finally became simple. And that is the countdown, from a Belgian strip in Germany to land inside land inside land.
scenes.headline: Maps Made Simple

scenes.narration: Which brings us back to the start: your cycle path is Belgian land, but German villages sit on both sides of it.
scenes.headline: Back To Belgium

scenes.narration: Next video: time zones that make no sense, including Nepal's, which sits fifteen minutes ahead of India's.
scenes.headline: Next: Strange Time Zones
